local.heading: Daphne is Baldwin County's biggest city, and new neighbors keep moving in.
paragraphs: Daphne sits on the Eastern Shore of Mobile Bay, with Spanish Fort to the north and Fairhope to the south, about 11 miles east of Mobile along I-10. The 2020 census made it the most populous city in Baldwin County. Census estimates released in 2026 show the city added about 3,850 residents since 2020, part of a county that ranks among the Southeast's top population gainers while neighboring Mobile County loses people.

Much of that growth is subdivisions east of Highway 98 and up toward I-10, built over the last 20 to 30 years. Closer to the water are Olde Towne Daphne and Lake Forest, where the golf course winds through the neighborhood and the yacht club sits on the bay. A family that just closed on a house doesn't have a plumber, a dentist or a lawn crew yet. They search on a phone, and a company with a clear site and real local reviews has the edge.

The business side of town follows the highways. I-10 has three exits into town, at US 98, US 90 and AL 181, and shopping centers like Jubilee Square on US 90 draw drivers from across the Eastern Shore. Infirmary Health has a surgery center and a diagnostic clinic on US 90, and Thomas Hospital is about five miles south in Fairhope. Search for a dentist from a parking lot on US 90 and Google lines up offices in Daphne, Spanish Fort and Fairhope together.

Daphne calls itself the Jubilee City, after the jubilees, when crab, shrimp and other sea life suddenly wash up along the bay shoreline. Each October the Eastern Shore Chamber of Commerce and the city put on the Jubilee Festival of Arts, which moved for good to Lott Park in Olde Towne Daphne in 2026 with more than 140 artists and a market for local food makers. The rest of the year, Main Street shops depend on locals and on people coming over from Mobile, and both groups look you up before they drive over.

industries.heading: Who we build for in Daphne
industries.intro: New subdivisions, a medical cluster on US 90 and a commuter population that drives to Mobile shape which local businesses need the web most.

items.name: Home services for new subdivisions
items.body: Roofers, HVAC, plumbers, pool companies and landscapers working the newer neighborhoods off Highway 98 and County Road 64. Storm-repair pages should be ready before hurricane season, not written after the first big blow.

items.name: Medical, dental and therapy offices
items.body: Practices along US 90 and US 98 compete with Infirmary Health's outpatient sites and with offices in Fairhope. Patients want insurance details, provider bios and a way to request a visit without calling during work.

items.name: Restaurants and shops
items.body: Places on Main Street in Olde Towne and in the centers near the I-10 exits. Hours, menus and photos have to match on the site and the Google profile, because people check both before they pick a place for dinner.

items.name: Real estate agents and lenders
items.body: People moving to the Eastern Shore research neighborhoods and schools from out of town. Area guides for Daphne, Spanish Fort and Fairhope give them a reason to call you instead of a national listing site.

items.name: Professional firms
items.body: Accountants, attorneys and insurance agents serving families who commute to Mobile. A clean site with clear services and an easy contact form turns a referral into an appointment.

includes.title: Ready for storm season

includes.title: Tap to call for the I-10 commute
includes.body: A lot of residents here drive to Mobile and back. Fast mobile pages, a call button at the top and a two-field form fit someone checking you out at a red light on US 98.

includes.title: Local SEO built in
includes.body: Titles, schema and your Google Business Profile all say the same thing about where you are and who you serve, so Google can match you to Daphne searches from day one.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Daphne businesses
paragraphs: We're based in Villa Rica, Georgia, a good drive from the Eastern Shore. So we work the way most of our out-of-town clients like: a video call to start, a working draft of the site you can tap through on your phone, and changes made from your notes. If a project needs us on site, we'll plan the trip with you.
You talk to the two people who build the site and run the SEO, start to finish. When your hours change or a storm closes you for a day, you send a text and we handle it.

faqs.q: How much does web design in Daphne, AL cost?
faqs.a: Most Daphne businesses start with our Local Marketing Package: $297 a month, month to month, with no contract. It includes local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (your ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Can a Daphne business show up ahead of Mobile companies?
faqs.a: For searches made on the Eastern Shore, it often can. Google puts a lot of weight on where the searcher is. A site that says plainly you serve Daphne, backed by a complete Google profile and reviews from local customers, holds its own against bigger Mobile companies that never mention Baldwin County.

faqs.q: Should my site mention Spanish Fort and Fairhope too?
faqs.a: If you work there, yes. Customers on the Eastern Shore move between all three towns, and Google treats each one as its own search. We give each town you serve its own page with real details, and leave out towns you don't cover.

faqs.q: Can you update my site fast when a storm hits?
faqs.a: Yes. Send us a text with your closure or emergency hours and we update the site notice and your Google profile. For roofers and other contractors, we can also turn on storm-repair ads after a storm if you want them.

faqs.q: Do I need to meet with you in person?
faqs.a: No. We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, and most of our Eastern Shore projects run on video calls and drafts you review on your phone. If sitting down together would help the project, we'll plan a trip.

faqs.q: What if I already have a website?
faqs.a: We start by checking what it does well. If it already ranks for useful searches, we keep those pages and their addresses. Often a rebuild is quicker than patching an old theme, and the website that comes with the package covers it.
